# ossl-fuku-transfer


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This project studies how well CNN models of soil mid-infrared (MIR)
spectra transfer from the [Open Soil Spectral Library
(OSSL)](https://explorer.soilspectroscopy.org/), measured on Bruker
instruments, to soil spectra from Fukushima, measured on a Thermo
Nicolet. A model can reach state-of-the-art accuracy on OSSL and still
fail on spectra from another spectrometer. This project measures how
large that gap is, and what causes it.

## Questions

- Zero-shot transfer: how well does a model trained on OSSL predict
  exchangeable potassium (Kex), cation exchange capacity (CEC) and
  organic carbon for the Fukushima samples, with no fine-tuning?
- Cause of the gap: similar losses across properties point to the
  instrument, for example baseline or scatter. Different losses point to
  specific bands or to the soil population. A PCA fitted on OSSL
  compares the Fukushima spectra with KSSL Andisols and with the rest of
  KSSL.
- Fine-tuning: how many Fukushima samples does a pretrained model need
  to reach a given R², compared with a model trained on Fukushima
  samples only?

## Set-up

The project uses the soilspec packages
([soilspecdl](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdl),
[soilspecdata](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdata) and
[soilspectfm](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspectfm)) as editable
installs from sibling folders:

    soilspec/
      ossl-fuku-transfer/
      soilspecdl/
      soilspecdata/
      soilspectfm/

Clone the four repositories into one folder, then, in
`ossl-fuku-transfer/`:

``` sh
uv sync --extra dev
```

The Fukushima data is not public. This repository does not contain it.
With access to it, put it in `data/fukushima/` in the workspace folder,
beside the project folders, or set `SOILSPEC_DATA` to the folder that
holds `fukushima/`. `nbdev-test` skips the cells that read the data. Run
`nbdev-test --flags fukudata` to include them.
